context: Route both the recommendation text and the Prompt default through benchbox.core.benchmark_registry.get_presort_table_configs, so benchmark knowledge stays in the registry. List both behavior deltas explicitly in the PR body.
description: benchbox/cli/tuning.py:781 prints 'Recommended for TPCH: l_shipdate, l_orderkey (for lineitem)' and :786 hardcodes default='l_shipdate' if benchmark.lower()=='tpch' else ''. The registry is now the owner of presort defaults after one-engine-core-run-service w5 (#1562): get_presort_table_configs('tpch') returns {'lineitem': [{'name': 'l_shipdate', 'order': 'asc'}]} and ('tpcds') returns {'store_sales': [{'name': 'ss_sold_date_sk', 'order': 'asc'}]}. l_orderkey appears in neither, so the interactive wizard has been recommending a sort column that benchbox run --presort does not apply. Two behavior deltas follow from routing the wizard through get_presort_table_configs: (1) the hint drops l_orderkey, correcting a hint that disagreed with the feature it describes; (2) TPC-DS gains a prefilled default of ss_sold_date_sk where it previously offered an empty string. Deliberately NOT resolved by adding l_orderkey to the registry -- that would silently change what --presort does to real benchmark runs. Found while closing verification rung 4 of one-engine-core-run-service.

preserves.behavior: --presort runtime behavior is unchanged: registry presort_table_configs values must not be edited to make the wizard hint match.
Benchmarks with no registry presort defaults still offer an empty prompt default rather than erroring.

verifications.description: No hardcoded benchmark sort columns in the wizard
verifications.expected: Wizard defaults come from the registry.
